MR JUSTICE ASHOK S.KINAGI
ORAL ORDER
The petitioner aggrieved by the order dated 28.03.2024, in Crl.Misc.809/2018 by the V Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru, filed the present revision petition.

entities.text: Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru
entities.label: JUDGE

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of this revision petition are as under:
The petitioner married the respondent on 15.08.2014 in Sri.Venkateshwara Kalyana Mantapa, Saraswathapur, Dharwad, as per the customs prevailing in their community.
The petitioner and respondent have led their marital life for a few weeks.
Thereafter, a dispute arises between the petitioner and respondent.
The respondent has been residing in her parent's house since 06.04.2017.
The respondent issued a legal notice for restitution of conjugal rights.
The petitioner replied to the legal notice and sought mutual divorce from the respondent.
The respondent filed a petition under Section 9 of The Hindu NC: 2024:KHC:53265 Marriage Act, 1955 (for short 'the HMA') in M.C.No.6024/2018.
The petitioner filed a petition for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1) (ia) of HMA in M.C.No.6626/2021.
The respondent filed a petition for maintenance in Crl.Misc.No.809/2018 on the file of V Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru.

entities.text: Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Family Court clubbed all the matters.

It is contended by the respondent that, the petitioner is working in Infosys as a Technology Leader, getting a handsome salary of Rs.1 lakh, and he is residing in his own house measuring 60 X 40 ft., and he has rented two houses on the Ist floor and getting rents.
The petitioner's father has two sites in Yemmiganur and commercial complexes.
It is contended that the respondent is not working.
Her father is a retired Government employee, and all his retirement benefits have been spent for the respondent's marriage, and all the family members are depend on the pension of her father.
It is contended that the petitioner abandoned/deserted the respondent and he has not made any arrangements for NC: 2024:KHC:53265 the respondent's maintenance.
Hence, the respondent filed the petition for maintenance.
3. The petitioner filed the objections denying the averments made in the petition.
It is stated that the respondent has narrated the facts, in his petition in M.C.No.6626/2021.
It is admitted that the respondent has been staying with her parents since April 2017.
It is denied that the entire family depends on the pension of her father.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: The Family Court clubbed all the matters and recorded common evidence.
The petitioner was examined as PW.1 and marked 3 documents as Exs.P1 to 3, and the respondent was examined as RW.1 and marked 14 documents as Exs.R1 to 14.

The Family Court, after recording the evidence,
hearing on both sides and on the assessment of oral and documentary evidence, dismissed the petition filed by the petitioner in M.C.No.6626/2021, and the petition filed by the respondent in M.C.No.6024/2018 was allowed and directed the petitioner NC: 2024:KHC:53265 to take back the respondent to his matrimonial home within two months from the date of the judgment to lead a happy marital life.

The petition filed by the respondent in Crl.Misc.No.809/2018 filed under Section 125 of Cr.P.C., (144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023) was allowed and directed the petitioner to pay maintenance of Rs.30,000/- p.m., to the respondent from the date of petition till her lifetime.
The petitioner, aggrieved by the order dated 28.03.2024 passed in Crl.Misc.No.809/2018, filed this revision petition.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the respondent.
6.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Family Court committed an error in awarding maintenance of Rs.30,000/- p.m.,
He submits that the Family Court has not properly appreciated the evidence and documents produced by the parties.

He submits that the respondent lodged a criminal case against the petitioner and his family members for the offences NC: 2024:KHC:53265 punishable under Section 498A of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the D.P.Act.
He submits that the respondent has suppressed the educational qualification, stating that she is a B.E graduate and gainfully employed before the marriage.
He submits that the maintenance awarded by the Family Court is exorbitant.
Hence, on these grounds, prays to allow the revision petition.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent submits that the petitioner deserted the respondent in April 2017, and she is residing with her parents.
The respondent's father is a retired employee and getting a meagre pension, and the entire family depends on the pension.
He submits that the petitioner has not made any arrangements to maintain the respondent.
The petitioner is working as a Technology Leader in Infosys and getting a handsome salary.
He submits that the maintenance awarded by the Family Court is just and proper and does not call for any interference.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to dismiss the revision petition.
Perused the records and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
9. There is no dispute regarding the relationship between the petitioner and respondent as a husband and wife.
Their marriage was performed on 15.08.2014, as per the customs prevailing in their community.
The petitioner and respondent have led their marital life for a few weeks.
Thereafter, the dispute arises between the petitioner and respondent.
The respondent lodged a criminal case against the petitioner and his family members.
The relationship between the petitioner and respondent were strained.
The respondent started residing in her parent's house in April 2017.
The respondent issued a legal notice under Section 9 of the HMA, as per Ex.R.10.
The petitioner replied to the legal notice.

sentences.text: As a counter blast to the petition filed by the respondent, the petitioner filed a petition for dissolution of marriage in M.C.No.6626/2021.
The petitioner was examined as PW.1.
He reiterated the averments made in the petition in M.C.No.6626/2021 in the examination-in chief and produced the documents.

Ex.P1 is the marriage photo, Ex.P2 is the marriage invitation card and Ex.P3 is the certified copy of the FIR, which discloses that the respondent lodged a criminal case against the petitioner and his family members for the offence punishable under Section 498A of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
During the cross examination, PW.1 admits that he had received notice as per Ex.R.10, and he filed a divorce petition at Hyderabad.

A question was put to PW.1, that the respondent is ready to dwell with him, and at the instigation of his parents, he is avoiding; PW.1 stated that he is not ready to take her back because of her attitude.
He also admitted that before the marriage, the respondent was working in Bengaluru and after marriage, without option, she had resigned from her job.
10. In rebuttal, the respondent examined herself as RW.1.
She reiterated the averments made in the petition NC: 2024:KHC:53265 Crl.Misc.No.809/2018.
In support of her contention, she has produced the documents.
Ex.R1 is the Marriage Invitation Card, Ex.R2 is the certified copy of the Lagna Pathrike, Ex.R3 is the certified copy of gold purchase receipt, Ex.R4 is the bank statement,

Ex.R5 is the certificate of marriage registration, Ex.R6 is the certified copy of the medical bills,
Ex.R7 is the certified copy of the gold purchase bills, Exs.R8 and 9 are the certified copies of the FIR and complaint.
Ex . R10
is the office copy of the legal notice issued by the respondent to the petitioner calling upon the petitioner to take her back.
Exs.R11 and 12 are the reply notices.
Ex. R13
is the certified copy of the registered gift deed.
Ex . R14
is the registered partition letter, and Ex.R14(a) is the translation copy of Ex.R14.

Nothing has been elicited in the cross examination to disbelieve the evidence of RW.1.
11.
It is clear from the records that the marriage of the petitioner was performed with the respondent, and both have led a marital life for a few weeks.
Thereafter, a - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:53265 dispute arose between the petitioner and respondent.
The respondent issued a legal notice for conjugal rights to the petitioner.
The petitioner replied to the legal notice and refused to join the respondent's company.
The respondent filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights in M.C.No.6024/2018 and also lodged a criminal case against the petitioner and his family members as per Ex.P3.
Admittedly, the respondent has been residing in her parent's house since April 2017.
The petitioner has not made any arrangement to maintain the respondent.
The petitioner and respondent both have filed an affidavit of assets and liabilities.
The perusal of the affidavit of assets and liabilities filed by the respondent, it discloses that, the respondent has no source of income for maintaining herself.

From the perusal of the affidavit of assets and liabilities filed by the petitioner, it discloses his educational qualification as B.Tech (Mechanical) and his salary is Rs.1,13,016/- p.m., and home take salary is Rs.88,823/-.
He has a personal loan of Rs.20,00,000/- and EMI of Rs.43,224/-.

Admittedly, the respondent is residing in Mr Ravindra Kumar Uppara Gummala vs Mrs. Soumya on 6 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55787987/
4 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:53265 Bengaluru without a job.

sentences.text: She requires the minimum sum of Rs.30,000/- for livelihood in Bengaluru.
The Family Court, considering the petitioner's monthly income, has awarded maintenance of Rs.30,000/-.
The petitioner, as a husband, is legally and morally liable/bound to maintain the respondent.
The petitioner cannot avoid maintaining the respondent.
The Family Court, considering the material on record, was justified in passing the impugned order.
Hence, I do not find any error in the impugned order.

12. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The revision petition is dismissed.
